title: Prescriptive rewrite: every chapter re-read under ADR-0032, ratchet to zero
description:
Umbrella for the review ADR-0032 started. The set became prescriptive and implementation-agnostic on 2026-09-12 (spec-repo PR #1, merge c6354f3); the rules landed there and each chapter is now re-read under them, one pull request per chapter, in dependency order.

READ FIRST, every ticket: docs/adr/0032-specification-is-prescriptive-and-implementation-agnostic.md (the decision, the refactor test, the fate of each chapter), README.md 'Requirement conventions' and 'How compliance is measured', AGENTS.md.

The refactor test: a sentence is a requirement only if a rewrite that keeps every byte on disk, every byte on the wire and every observable behaviour identical CANNOT violate it. On-disk shapes, wire shapes, protocol facts and persisted/serialized type names stay. Function and method names, crate and file paths, line numbers, frameworks, the fork pin, the actor mechanism go; their behaviours and invariants stay as requirements.

Done-condition shared by every chapter ticket:
1. Every requirement in the chapter re-read, not re-moded: states a behaviour observable at a boundary (federation/gateway, seed, frontend, durability); says what the wallet SHOULD do, so where today's code differs the requirement changes and the code gains a finding; buildable from the text alone.
2. Requirements that described only a codebase fact are withdrawn: id removed, row added to README.md 'Withdrawn identifiers' (Identifier | Was | Why it went). Never renumber, never reuse.
3. New behaviour a re-read exposes gets the next free id in its namespace.
4. tools/codebase-refs-baseline.txt: the chapter's line lowered to its new count (target 0) in the same PR.
5. bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0, run unpiped, before and after.
6. The PR description carries a HAND-OFF LIST for the code repository: each Fn in douglaz/fedimint-wallets/docs/open-findings.md whose sense changes (gap-vs-decision becomes non-conformance-vs-requirement), each new non-conformance a strengthened requirement creates, and each finding a withdrawn requirement orphans. A code-repo bead is cut from that list when the PR merges; it is not this ticket's work.
7. One PR per chapter; the two review bots (Codex connector, CodeRabbit) run on every push; address findings, then merge.

Order (blocking edges): 00 → 01 → 02 → 03 → 05 → 06 → 04 → 07 → 08 → 09 → 10 → final pass. Persistence before allocator because ALC cites STO properties; API after the lifecycle because 04 is the wire view of 03.

title: Chapter 02 fedimint integration: rewrite under ADR-0032 (fork pin out, patched behaviours in)
description:
Rewrite 02-fedimint-integration.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 35 lines — second heaviest. This chapter is where 'environment vs codebase' bites: the Fedimint federation and gateway protocols are presupposed and cited freely; the SDK's internal API is not.
Decided in ADR-0032:
- FMI-1 (the douglaz/fedimint fork pin at a revision) and FMI-2 (any repoint carries every patch) GO. Each behaviour the three patches provide becomes its own FMI requirement: iroh long-poll bound, recovery complete-or-fail, single-share TPE correctness. Hand-off: F19 (the pin) becomes 'satisfied by fork patch, not upstream' compliance notes on those requirements; F20 (lnv2 claim-retry / reclaim_receive) is a non-conformance against a new requirement that a Stranded move has a recovery path — write that requirement.
- FMI-7 seed derivation STAYS and becomes normative with the derivation stated, no SDK names: two implementations must derive the same keys or recovery is not implementation-independent.
- FMI-11 keeps the routing_info exchange (protocol) and loses 'pooled HTTP client'; F45 (SSRF egress) is a non-conformance against a new SEC/FMI requirement restricting egress — coordinate with the 07 ticket, decide the owner here and cite from 07.
- FMI-13 gateway_serves_route(to, from, gw), FMI-36 MultiClient::new/ConnectorRegistry, FMI-3 'four modules on one ClientBuilder' — restate as behaviour (which modules a joined federation must expose; how transport is decided by invite and config).
- FMI-10 'the SDK's list_gateways(None)' — the vetted list is defined by ADR-0029 (threshold-vetted, read per guardian); write the requirement to the ADR, F6 becomes the non-conformance.
- FMI-19 'enforced at the pin, on the wrong ordering' — descriptive of a defect; the requirement is the correct ordering (component-wise), the current behaviour is a finding.
Hand-off: F6, F19, F20, F45 change sense; possibly new findings for FMI-19.
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 03 operation lifecycle: rewrite under ADR-0032 (invariants stay, actor goes)
description:
Rewrite 03-operation-lifecycle.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 22 lines. The chapter's substance — admission, execution, resumption, terminalization, the four killpoints, supersession, reconcile — is behaviour and stays. What goes is the mechanism: 'through the actor', 'Runtime::tick', 'Runtime::do_move', 'the standalone path bypasses the actor' (OPS-12, OPS-5 etc). Per ADR-0032 the invariants are requirements: one serialized admission point; one live key per allocator goal; agent work admitted nowhere else; generation-fenced writes; no operation's network IO on the admission point. State them as MUSTs on the wallet, not on an actor.
The standalone tick admission exception (ADR-0031, CONTEXT.md Engine) is behaviour and stays.
OPS-39 (RefuseReason by message substring) is a wire contract nobody documented as one — under the prescriptive posture decide: either the reason codes are the contract (write the table as normative, message text informative) or the substrings are; recommend codes. Hand-off: F37 changes sense.
F42 (standalone probe bypasses actor) and F44 (user move attaches to a probe leg) are non-conformances against the admission invariants once written; F8 (refused-after-commit row on the planned pair) against the ledger-correctness requirement — say which requirement each violates in the hand-off.
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 05 persistence: rewrite under ADR-0032 (on-disk shapes stay, write paths go)
description:
Rewrite 05-persistence.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 43 lines — the heaviest chapter, and the one where the refactor test does the most work. ON DISK STAYS: two stores (STO-1), the advisory lock file (STO-2), partition prefixes (STO-3), the seed encoding (STO-4), key tags and value encodings (STO-5), correlation/idempotency key shapes (STO-6), every persisted row field by field (STO-9..15, 26), the serde-rules-as-encoding (STO-29..31: a field added to a persisted type MUST decode when absent; no persisted type rejects unknown fields). These are an upgrade-in-place contract.
GOES: 'enforced by the pure advance function' (STO-16), 'repair_ledger scans' (STO-24), wallet_core::MoveRecord paths, 'fedimint's raw byte transactions' as mechanism (STO-7 — keep the atomicity property), which writer performs a write. Keep every PROPERTY: write discipline, CAS fencing (STO-8), O(1) sequence assignment (STO-18), one current row per correlation key (STO-20), the Agent occurrence floor (STO-21..23), unreadable rows never fence automation (STO-22), terminal immutability, the OPS-24 ordering.
STO-32 ('greenfield in one respect... unverified against the long-running deployment's store') is deployment content: the requirement is that the two fields decode when absent like every other; F38 is the check against one store and stays a code-repo item. STO-19 'full ascending scan, reverses' is an algorithm — keep the observable (history is newest-first, paged by before_seq), drop the scan.
Hand-off: F12 (no app-state backup) — decide whether a snapshot/restore is a requirement (ADR-0025 says the seed is the backup unit; Restore is an operator action) or stays a code-repo task; F38, F41 sense; F7 (committed route not persisted) is a non-conformance against the Committed route requirement (cite ADR-0030).
See the epic for the shared done-condition.

title: Chapter 06 allocator and automation: rewrite under ADR-0032
description:
Rewrite 06-allocator-and-automation.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 22 lines. The decision core is already stated as a pure function over a snapshot — keep that as a requirement (determinism, no IO) without naming decide(). Route economics, scoring, probes, discovery, evacuation, the tick, the scheduler cycle and the readiness signal are behaviour.
Watch for: ALC-15 'unreachable in production' (the scorer's activity buckets) — a prescriptive set does not carry dead branches; either the buckets are required behaviour with a stated input, or the requirement is withdrawn. ALC-19 (two evacuation leads with one name) — decide the requirement: one lead, or two with distinct names; F36 becomes the non-conformance. ALC-45..49 (readiness, the fourth invisible suppression, eight fail-closed paths without a ledger row, the light probe four times per cycle) are currently written as descriptions of defects: rewrite each as the requirement (every suppression reported on /v1/health; every fail-closed path leaves a row; the light probe runs once per cycle or the count is a stated requirement) and hand off F32, F33, F34 as non-conformances. 'Runtime::watch_once is a dev/test harness with no production caller' fails the refactor test — withdraw or restate as 'no host schedules through anything but the engine's cycle'. ALC-50 (cfg(test) seams) is codebase — withdraw.
The F1 shortfall-with-no-signal: requirement = every withheld funding decision is recorded (see 00 ticket); F1 non-conformance. F10 (no aggregate ceiling) — decide whether an aggregate exposure cap is a requirement (recommend yes, since exposure otherwise scales with joins) and hand off. F15 (conflict-suppressed goals not in status) likewise.
Hand-off: F1, F10, F14, F15, F32, F33, F34, F36 change sense; F3 (hop unbuilt) is a non-conformance against ADR-0029's requirements — make sure the hop requirement is written here, not only in the ADR.

title: Chapter 07 security: rewrite under ADR-0032
description:
Rewrite 07-security-requirements.md prescriptively. Baseline today: 3 lines — light on codebase refs, heavy on 'what is actually enforced — including what is not', which is the descriptive posture in its purest form. Every 'not enforced' becomes either a requirement (and a finding in the hand-off) or a decided non-goal citing its ADR.
Known items:
- The seed at rest (SEC-n citing ADR-0026). Write the requirement at the level ADR-0026 DECIDED, no further: the seed MUST NOT be stored in plaintext; it is protected by AEAD over the stored entropy under a key not stored beside it; when the key source is unavailable at start the wallet fails closed and never falls back to plaintext; mnemonic export and restore-mnemonic keep working. The KEY SOURCE (operator passphrase with a memory-hard KDF vs KMS/HSM) is a RECOMMENDATION in ADR-0026 'to ratify in the implementation bead', not a decision — do not ratify it through this rewrite. If the 07 PR wants to settle it, propose an ADR-0026 amendment in the PR and let it be accepted on its own; until then the requirement is silent on key derivation. F11 is the non-conformance.
- SEC-17 (no ADR records the per-guardian response bound) — write the bound as a requirement or withdraw the sentence.
- SEC-20 / DEF-22 (deployment identity not in tracked files) is a code-repo hygiene rule about one tree, not a wallet requirement — withdraw SEC-20 here (DEF-22 handled by the 09 ticket).
- SEC-24 (an id alone carries no guardian endpoints) stays.
- F45 egress restriction: the owner is decided by the 02 ticket; cite it from here.
Threat model: keep, as the frame the requirements answer. Remove any 'today the code does X' hedges.
Hand-off: F11, F21 (deployment identity in git history — code-repo only, no spec requirement), F45 sense.

title: Chapter 09 known defects: keep the prohibitions, drop the provenance

title: Chapter 10 conformance: the normative scenario suite
description:
Rewrite 10-conformance-checklist.md as the normative scenario suite (ADR-0032). Baseline today: 11 lines. Each surviving CNF-n is a scenario — given / when / then — at the wallet's boundaries, names the requirements it demonstrates ('demonstrates: ALC-20, DEF-21'), and carries NO result: no checkbox, no commit hash, no test function name, no run date, no gate command line. Add the sentence that makes it normative: a conformant implementation MUST pass every scenario.
Scenarios are stated against the wallet's ENVIRONMENT — two federations, their gateways, a Lightning node, a crash at a named point — never against a harness. devimint is the reference implementation's harness and lives in the code repository; a scenario does not name it, any harness that produces the given state is admissible, and how the code repository realises each scenario is its conformance-results file's business.
WITHDRAW (README rows): process discipline CNF-1, CNF-2, CNF-3, CNF-30, CNF-39, CNF-40 (to the code repo's AGENTS.md — most already there); build/unit results CNF-4, CNF-5; work items wearing a CNF id: CNF-45 (human reading of four boundaries, F26), CNF-46 (sidecar, F27), CNF-47 (seed re-encryption, F11), CNF-48 (restore drill) — their Fn already track them. Every other unchecked box is either a scenario nobody has run (keep as a scenario; the code repo's results say unrun) or a finding (withdraw, hand off).
ADD scenarios the chapter rewrites exposed as missing: the flat-cap regression DEF-25 / F22 (an evacuation whose parameters discriminate the cap basis), the after-receive-commit killpoint F25, the recovery FAILURE path F24, delivered≠ask at the pre-mint gate F23. Each is a scenario here and a non-conformance ('scenario not yet runnable/passing') in the hand-off.
Verify: every requirement in 02–08 that claims to be demonstrable cites a CNF, and every CNF cites at least one requirement. Baseline to 0.
Hand-off: F22, F23, F24, F25, F26 sense; the checkbox state at c6354f3 as the code repo's initial conformance-results file.

title: OPS-20 follow-up: the planned-cap fallback for an Evacuate row without fee_cap is looser than the enforced cap
description:
Raised by CodeRabbit on spec-repo PR #7 (chapter 05) and deferred there because OPS-20 (03) owns
the precedence. OPS-20's cap precedence for reassembly is artifact > cached (only when the cache
holds a receive or send operation id) > planned. A committed receive operation whose MoveMeta
carries no `fee_cap` (a row an older build wrote; STO-33 says absent decodes as none, never zero)
therefore falls back to the intent's PLANNED cap. For an `Evacuate` the planned cap is
`fee_cap_components.at(planned amount)`, and the planned amount is larger than the delivered net,
so the reconstructed cap is LOOSER than the cap that was enforced at the sized net — the pairing
DEF-4 / STO-17 exists to prevent (an auditor recomputing the cap from an amount nobody received).

Decide, in 03: should the fallback for an `Evacuate` (an intent carrying `fee_cap_components`)
be `fee_cap_components.at(meta.amount)` — the leg's own `amount` IS on the metadata (STO-33),
so the enforced cap is reconstructible without the cache — with the planned cap only for an
action without components? Or state that such a row is not rebuildable and the pay step
re-checks under the planned cap (OPS-26 already re-quotes both legs against rec.fee_cap)?

Owner: OPS-20 (and OPS-26 if the re-check wording changes). Land as one clause; cite ADR-0029
("the cap enforced at that net") and CONTEXT.md **Delivered net**. Any code that falls back to
the planned cap today becomes a non-conformance in the code repo's open-findings.md.
Gate: bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0 before and after; 03's ratchet baseline stays 0.
close_reason: Landed in spec-repo PR #14 (e360604): OPS-20's cap fallback is the action's cap rule at the reassembled amount; OPS-25 cites it; code-repo bead br-ops20-capless-leg-fallback-nb8 tracks the implementation check

title: Four-model review 2026-09-23: blockers and majors
description:
Umbrella for the findings of the 2026-09-23 independent review of the whole set (Fable, Opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol; same prompt, read-only, full corpus at cd4ea86). Consensus verdict: NOT BUILDABLE as written — an implementer with only this repository and the public Fedimint SDK cannot produce a wallet compliant with every MUST at once. Consolidated report with every citation: ~/spec-review/CONSOLIDATED.md (raw per-model reports beside it).

Shared done-condition for every child: (1) the contradiction or gap is resolved in the OWNING requirement, everywhere else cites the id (README, One owner per rule); (2) a decision nobody has taken goes to 11-open-questions.md and the set stays silent, per AGENTS.md; (3) a new rule gets the next free id in its namespace, withdrawn ids get a README row; (4) where the requirement can be demonstrated, 10-conformance-checklist.md gains or amends the scenario and the requirement cites it; (5) bash tools/check-all.sh exit 0, unpiped, before and after; (6) any requirement whose sense changes for the existing implementation is listed as a hand-off for the code repository's docs/open-findings.md.

Priority 0 children are the three blockers; priority 1 are the majors. Every finding marked verified was re-checked against the cited lines by the orchestrating session; plausible ones were not.

## Corrected after the 2026-09-23 four-model bead review (reports: ~/spec-review/beads-{fable,opus,astra,sol}.md)
Accounting corrections: the first review's verdict was 2 × BUILDABLE WITH GAPS (Fable, Opus) and 2 × NOT BUILDABLE (Astra, Sol), not a consensus; the orchestrator sides with NOT BUILDABLE after verification. The SDK premise was wrong: /home/master/p/fedimint's origin is upstream fedimint/fedimint, and upstream v0.12.0+ has single-attempt send dedup (703a37e8f3f) and component-wise fee limits (d5febdf9d37); spec-bsd and spec-ezl were closed as false, and ADR-0032 already says fork patches become requirements and SDK versions are a code-repo fact. Blockers now: spec-dgj (OPS-45 vs killpoint 4), spec-azs (funds above the admitted cap), spec-cuw (retry double-send). spec-iym is major and decision-gated. spec-pcr merged into spec-1nc; spec-pz6 split into the assertion fixes and a coverage bead; spec-cuw split into retry safety and claimability. Downgraded to minor: spec-yot, spec-gke, spec-s9a, spec-11k, spec-hrb, spec-iq9. New: the claimability bead, 'trusted'/'probed', untyped persisted fields, user fee_cap defaults, ALC-29 counters, the preflight-failed probe session, the tick ledger order, FMI-42's minimum, the DOM-5/API-15 pair, the coverage bead. Real blocking edges are recorded with br dep; everything else is independent. Suggested order (Fable/Opus/Sol converge): money path first (dgj, cuw, azs, 5gn, 1nc, sn0, shy), then vocabulary and storage (trusted/probed, 0c8, yae, types, fee_cap), then surfaces (6w6, 22p, 9iq-if-wanted, 9iq, pe4, ee9), then automation (nwm, counters, probe session, order, 9c6, j8w, l1w, bqv, y0b), then the decision-gated three (iym, 11k, dn8), scenarios last.

title: SEC-25 seed encryption: decide the key source, add the slot layout STO, open a channel in HST-2/HST-3
description:
BLOCKER, 4/4 reviewers, verified. 07-security-requirements.md:101-126 (SEC-25): the seed MUST NOT be stored in plaintext, keyed from outside the store — yet the key source is ADR-0026's recommendation, not its decision; this requirement is silent on it, and the encrypted slot's layout is fixed under a STO identifier with that decision. That STO id does not exist. 05-persistence.md:48-51 (STO-4) defers the same way. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:19-24 (HST-2) owns the COMPLETE environment surface and 08:40-50 (HST-3) has five keys and MUST reject any other — no key-source row or key anywhere, so no compliant way for the key to reach the daemon. 08:97-104 (HST-6) serve order has no unseal step; HST-7 / ALC-40 require exit-and-supervisor-restart, which an interactive prompt cannot survive. 10-conformance-checklist.md:288-303 (CNF-47) and 00-overview.md:116-120 (OVR-14) require an old build to fail on the re-encrypted store, which needs a discriminator no STO rule defines. 11-open-questions.md:16-34 does not list the decision, against AGENTS.md (an untaken product decision goes to chapter 11).
Consequence: two implementations that guess differently write mutually unreadable client.db root slots; CNF-47 is non-portable; SEC-25, HST-2 and HST-3 cannot all be satisfied.
Fix: (a) add the key-source question to 11-open-questions.md now, and state in SEC-25 that HST-2/HST-3's enumerations are extended by that decision; (b) ADR deciding the key source (ADR-0026 option 1 variants: env var naming a passphrase file, KMS reference, interactive unseal); (c) new STO-n: discriminator/version byte, KDF and AEAD parameters, nonce, ciphertext, associated data; (d) the delivery row/key in HST-2 and/or HST-3; (e) an unseal / re-encrypt step in HST-6's order; (f) CNF-47 restated against the decided layout with fixed vectors.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
Severity: major, decision-gated (Opus, Astra, Sol: SEC-25 is 'silent' on the source, so an OS key facility, a fixed-path file or a TTY prompt is compliant; what is impossible is interoperability of the slot and a portable CNF-47). Do NOT add a sentence that HST-2/HST-3 are 'extended by that decision' — while the decision is open the set stays silent (AGENTS.md); Sol. Actionable now: ONLY step (a) — the chapter-11 entry naming the decision (key source, provisioning, unavailable-key behaviour, restart expectations under HST-7/ALC-40's exit-and-restart model, and whether an unattended unseal must succeed), and a note in SEC-25 that it is governed by that question. Blocked on the ADR: (b)-(f). When decided: STO-36 (next free STO; STO-32 withdrawn) owns the slot bytes — version/discriminator, AEAD, nonce, ciphertext, AAD, and KDF parameters only if the source is a passphrase; the discriminator MUST make an old build fail to decode (BIP-39 accepts 16-32-byte entropy, so a bare 32-byte ciphertext would decode as a 24-word seed — Opus); delivery surface = HST-2 row and/or HST-3 key AND the standalone flag in HST-10 (mnemonic / restore-mnemonic / standalone need the key too — Fable); an unseal step in HST-6 ('load the seed' may absorb it); CNF-47 restated with fixed vectors. Android's Keystore path (ADR-0011) is a second unowned mechanism — coordinate with spec-11k.

title: OPS-45 pre-fund admission at the fourth killpoint can terminalize a committed send (Invoiced not exempt)
description:
BLOCKER, Astra, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:259-264 (OPS-45): for Move and DirectInflow pre-fund admission runs BEFORE reassembly (OPS-20) and is skipped only when the cached record is trusted and its phase is Sending | Settled | Refunded | Failed | Stranded — Invoiced is not exempt. 03:100-103 (OPS-7): amount + fee_cap <= balance[from] - reservations.outbound(from), sampled fresh. 03:584 (OPS-28, fourth killpoint): send committed; the record lacks the send operation id — required resume is backfill, or a re-pay deduplicates to already in flight. 03:271-272: its refusal is Permanent and terminalizes the intent.
Scenario: a source holding just enough for amount + fee_cap; the send commits and debits it; the process dies before the send op id is written; on restart the record is Invoiced, OPS-45 runs the OPS-7 arithmetic on the debited balance, fails insufficient_after_reservations, and the intent is Failed while the outgoing contract is in flight. Contradicts OPS-28 exactly-once and CNF-12 (10:92).
Fix: for Move/DirectInflow run reassembly (discover committed artifacts by move_id / dedup) before pre-fund admission, or exempt Invoiced when the send is found committed; state which. Add a killpoint-4 scenario with a tightly funded source, once with the pre-receive draft cache present and once after cache loss.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; understated (Opus): a second trigger is the DESTINATION check — at killpoint 4 the swap may already have completed, so balance[to] already includes amount and OPS-7's 'balance[to] + reservations.inbound(to) + amount <= per_fed_cap' counts it twice (over_cap even with a well-funded source). DirectInflow has the same exposure: a crash after the invoice write but before the Awaiting write re-performs an Executing intent with cached phase Invoiced; if the payer already paid, the destination is double-counted. Corrected fix (one formulation, Sol; keyed on reassembled artifacts, not on the undefined 'trusted' — Fable, Opus): in OPS-45, for Move and DirectInflow run reassembly (OPS-20: cache, then the operation log by move_id / correlation key) BEFORE pre-fund admission; then skip the SOURCE arithmetic when the reassembled record has a send operation id (killpoints 2-3 still need it: the send is new funding), and skip the DESTINATION arithmetic when a receive artifact exists (invoice or receive operation id). Exempting every Invoiced record without the lookup is wrong (Astra): it would admit an unfunded invoice without the fresh checks. Owner OPS-45; OPS-19, OPS-7 ('again at perform time') and CONTEXT.md Reassembly keep citing it; OPS-35's optional pre-step backfill becomes irrelevant. Scenario here (not in the coverage bead): amend CNF-12 or add CNF-55 — killpoint 4 with a tight source, with the destination at cap minus amount, with the pre-receive draft cache present and lost.

title: FMI-17 send dedup (and FMI-30/38/39/41) describe the fork SDK, not upstream: make the guarantees wallet-enforced
description:
BLOCKER, Astra + Opus, verified for FMI-17 against the local checkout. 02-fedimint-integration.md:235-237 (FMI-17): an lnv2 send is deduplicated by an operation id derived from the invoice: one payment attempt per invoice per client; a second send MUST NOT fund a second outgoing contract. 03:347 (raw pay) and 03:151-153 (OPS-10, retry refused with this invoice already consumed its single payment attempt) rest on it. The local fork (bradleystachurski/fedimint, modules/fedimint-lnv2-client/src/lib.rs:567-570) pins the attempt index to 0 with the comment that older clients derived a fresh index per payment attempt; upstream master derives OperationId from (invoice, attempt) and lets a failed/refunded attempt be followed by a new one. An implementer on the public SDK therefore funds a second contract after an unrecorded, later-refunded send — exactly what FMI-17 forbids — and never sees the dead operation the text promises.
Opus lists the other rules the withdrawn FMI-1 recorded as fork patches: FMI-30 (complete-or-fail within 600 s of no progress), FMI-38 (5-minute bounded re-issued waits), FMI-39 (single-share decryption), FMI-41 (claim retried until expiry). Each is a legitimate requirement but presupposes SDK behaviour the public SDK may not have.
Fix: (a) make the no-second-attempt guarantee a wallet rule: persist the operation id before issuing the send (already the raw path's order) and refuse a second send of any invoice that has a recorded operation id regardless of the terminal, including after a missing artifact write; state the disposition of terminal failed/refunded sends explicitly; (b) a chapter-02 note (or a row per rule) naming which FMI behaviours an upstream SDK may not provide, so an implementer knows to enforce them above the SDK; (c) a restart scenario: send issued, artifact write lost, send refunded, restart — no second contract.
close_reason: Premise false (Opus, Astra, Sol; re-verified against /home/master/p/fedimint whose origin is upstream fedimint/fedimint): single-attempt lnv2 send dedup is upstream since v0.12.0 (commit 703a37e8f3f, 2026-07-10); the code repo's pin 72b1e5be has it too. FMI-17 and OPS-17 describe the public SDK. FMI-30/38/39/41 are already MUSTs on the wallet; whether an SDK release provides them is a code-repo finding, and a chapter-02 SDK-version note would fail the refactor test (ADR-0032). The fix's claim that the raw path persists the op id before the send was also wrong (OPS-17: issue, then persist; the hash lookup covers the crash window). Residual: FMI-17 says 'the protocol derives' where it is the client that derives (wording nit); the send-issued / artifact-lost / refunded / restart scenario moves to the coverage bead.

title: Gross-up: FMI-18 selects an over-crediting contract, FMI-15 requires never more; OPS-44 cites a nonexistent OPS-22 fixed point
description:
MAJOR, Astra, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:213-219 (FMI-15): the destination is credited amount ... never more, and possibly less by a bounded shortfall ... the best verified under-crediting candidate. 02:267-268 (FMI-18): gross_up(net, gateway_fee, fed_fee) is the smallest invoice amount such that contract = invoice - gw(invoice) and contract - fed(contract) >= net — the >= selects the over-crediting side when no exact solution exists, the case FMI-15 expressly contemplates. 03:449-450 (OPS-44): gross n up ... (FMI-18, OPS-22's fixed point); OPS-22 (03:502-513) defines no fixed point. OPS-23 (03:536) checks only equality of quoted and committed contracts, so it cannot catch an over-crediting quote.
Fix: one owner (FMI-18) with one mathematical contract: the exact solution when it exists, else the largest under-crediting candidate, the shortfall bound (one receive-fee step plus the mint output fee), and the no-solution case; correct the inequality; delete or define the fixed-point reference in OPS-44.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
MERGED with spec-pcr (all four reviewers: one arithmetic, one owner). spec-pcr's text follows.

--- spec-pcr ---
MAJOR, Astra, PLAUSIBLE. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:297 defines delivered net as invoice - receive_quote, what the destination is actually credited; 03:454 (OPS-44) sizes and enforces the cap on that arithmetic. 02-fedimint-integration.md:218 (FMI-15) admits the federation's mint output fee on the claim, which the lnv2 receive quote does not include. So the computed delivered net can exceed the real credit. 10-conformance-checklist.md:79 (CNF-10) tolerates a bounded shortfall while 10:87 (CNF-11) requires B to rise by exactly the amount, under an environment (10:20-27) that fixes no fee schedule.
Fix: define requested, quoted and credited amounts once and use the right one in each rule (cap enforcement on the quoted delivered net is fine if stated; balance assertions on the credited amount); rewrite CNF-11's assertion as a bound, or fix the fixture's fees so exactly is true, and say so.
--- end ---

Corrected fix, one change: FMI-18 owns the gross-up contract; FMI-15 owns the amount vocabulary. Define once: requested net, invoice (gross), incoming contract amount, gateway receive fee (the lnv2 quote), federation mint output fee on the claim (NOT in the quote, FMI-15:218), actual credited amount = invoice - receive_quote - mint_fee. FMI-18: exact solution when one exists; else the candidate whose CREDITED amount is the largest not exceeding the request (not the numerically largest invoice), ties to the smallest invoice; the shortfall bound (one receive-fee step + the mint output fee); the 5 000 msat minimum-contract restriction; the no-solution case. OPS-44 drops 'OPS-22's fixed point' (it exists only in CONTEXT.md:129, Delivered net); CONTEXT.md aligns. Caps: OVR-7 (00:55) says the enforced cap is 'computed from what the destination is actually credited', so ALC-21/OPS-44's invoice - receive_quote is a quoted proxy — either state that the cap basis is the quoted delivered net and amend OVR-7, or use the credited amount; do not leave both. CONTEXT.md:131 'Every ENFORCED fee cap is computed from the delivered net' vs OVR-7's funding-move planned-cap exception: OVR-7 owns, the glossary quotes it. Scenarios: the environment header (10:26-27 'rises by the amount … are exact'), CNF-9, CNF-11, CNF-12, CNF-42 all assert exact credits with no fee fixture — either fix the environment's mint output fee at 0 and say so in the header, or turn each 'exactly' into CNF-10's bound. Owners: FMI-15, FMI-18, ALC-21, OVR-7; cite from OPS-22/23/24/44, CNF-9/10/11/12/42.

title: Retry deletes the move record and orphans a still-claimable contract; re-claim is reachable only once the contract is expired
description:
MAJOR, Opus + Astra, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:151-163 (OPS-10): retry is refused only for a Stranded move; it deletes the cached move record, appends a fresh ledger row and repoints the key index. 02:328-335 (FMI-41): a funded incoming contract the wallet has not claimed MUST remain claimable ... an explicit re-claim, invocable for one operation by its operation key. 04-api-contract.md:580-584 (API-42): {key} names the operation whose contract reached a terminal non-claim. After a retry the key resolves to the new attempt and the old recv_op is gone, so the prior contract is unreachable by reclaim — breaks FMI-41. The retry also sends again while the first outgoing contract's position is unresolved (FMI-37 case b); HST-32's evidence preservation covers only Stranded.
Second half (Astra): FMI-41 retries a rejected claim until the contract's expiry has passed before Failure, and API-42 admits only terminal non-claims, so for the rejected-claim case reclaim becomes invocable exactly when it must answer not_claimable. The accepted-claim-then-issuance-failed case has already consumed the contract. No described path recovers the funds CONTEXT.md:296 promises (a delayed app open does NOT forfeit an already-settled payment).
Fix: (a) extend OPS-10's refusal to a Failed move or direct inflow whose receive terminal is Failure, or whose send terminal is Failure after funding, until a reclaim returned not_claimable; (b) keep the prior attempt's move record under an attempt-scoped key and let API-42 address an attempt (retry: correlation key or seq); (c) separate invoice/funding expiry from claimability of an already-funded contract and define a reachable recovery state with a scenario that demonstrates a successful re-claim.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
PROMOTED to blocker and SPLIT (Fable, Astra, Sol). THIS bead keeps the money-safety half: OPS-10 retry safety and prior-attempt addressability. The claimability half (FMI-41/API-42: a reachable re-claim before the contract is non-claimable, the funding-expiry vs claimability distinction) is now its own bead — see the child titled 'FMI-41 / API-42: re-claim is reachable only once the contract is expired'. Corrections: (1) the guard 'refuse retry until a reclaim returned not_claimable' is UNSAFE and circular (Astra, Sol): destination non-claimability says nothing about whether the SOURCE send was funded, and FMI-37 says the wallet cannot tell send case (a) from (b). Key the refusal on FMI-37's own anchor instead: OPS-10 refuses retry of a Failed move (or direct inflow) whose error begins 'send failed:' (the prefix HST-32 already fixes) until its outgoing contract's position is known (Refunded, or a preimage per FMI-23) — a one-sentence fix that closes the double-send. (2) 'Orphans the contract' is overstated (Astra): OPS-10 keeps 'two truthful rows', STO-15 keeps the op ids in them, STO-20 keeps older rows addressable by seq, and the client operation log survives; what is missing is a contract for API-42 to address an older attempt. Lighter than an attempt-scoped record key (which would be a new tag under STO-5's 'exactly thirteen tags', STO-29/30): let API-42 locate the receive operation by the attempt correlation keys in the operation log (STO-34: the key, then retry:<len>:<key>:<n>) — Opus. Owners: OPS-10, STO-34, API-42, HST-32.

title: OPS-22 over-cap raw receive persists the invoice first, and OPS-16 / API-21 then return it to the caller as payable
description:
MAJOR, Astra, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:385-388 (OPS-22, raw receive committed-fee check): actual > fee_cap -> persist the operation id and invoice FIRST, so the orphan is recorded, then Permanent. 03:302-304 (OPS-16): target invoice resolves as soon as the intent's invoice or the move record's invoice exists. 04-api-contract.md:297-299 (API-21): 409 failed only for terminal WITHOUT an invoice. So the payer receives an invoice the wallet judged over cap, including on resubmission; meanwhile the terminalized intent releases its reservation (OPS-9 reserves only non-terminal intents).
Fix: distinguish a recorded orphan artifact from a publishable invoice (a flag on the intent or a separate field); API-21 returns 409 for any terminal intent whatever artifacts it holds; state what the wallet does if the orphan invoice is nonetheless paid (it is a funded incoming contract: FMI-41 claim path, and the fee actually charged is recorded).

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
Corrections: the cited rule at 03:385-388 is OPS-18 (raw Receive), not OPS-22 (all four). The race is before terminalization (Astra): the artifact write wakes invoice waiters, so the rejected invoice is published before the Permanent outcome lands. '409 for any terminal intent' is WRONG for Done (Opus, Astra): API-21 promises 'Re-submitting the same key re-yields the same invoice' and OPS-8 deduplicates Done — make it 409 for a Failed intent, or (lighter, no new field) let OPS-16's invoice target resolve only for a non-Failed intent, and require publication eligibility to be decided atomically before waking waiters. Also state what a retry (OPS-10 refuses only a Failed pay with an op id, so this Failed receive IS retryable) does with the live orphan invoice, and what observes and claims the incoming contract if the orphan is paid out of band (FMI-41; the claimability bead) while preserving the failure evidence and never initiating another payment. Owners: OPS-18, OPS-16, API-21.

title: Supersession marker: OPS-31 says the retired parent keeps it, CNF-24 asserts it is cleared
description:
MAJOR, Astra, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:617-620 (OPS-31): the marker is cleared by ... the exchange (the retired parent keeps it). 10-conformance-checklist.md:145-147 (CNF-24): the parent is Failed as superseded with its marker cleared. 01-domain-model.md:181 requires preservation of the parent's evidence.
Fix: choose one persisted-state contract. Evidence preservation argues for: the parent keeps the marker, inactive because the row is terminal; the child never inherits it. Say it once in OPS-31, make CNF-24 assert exactly that, and test retained evidence separately from active status.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; the resolution stands (parent keeps the field, inactive because terminal; child never inherits it; API-33's evacuation_refusal_active already implies the field survives). One addition (Astra): fix OPS-31's projection too — it currently yields false for a readable intent WITHOUT a marker and leaves a terminal intent WITH retained evidence uncovered; align with API-33: true only for the live Pending evacuation carrying the marker, false for every other readable intent, omitted only when no intent is readable. CNF-24's assertion lands here, not in the coverage bead. DOM-20, STO-25 align.

title: Send fee admission is not bound to the contract actually funded (SDK re-fetches routing_info inside send)
description:
MAJOR, Astra, PLAUSIBLE (SDK-dependent, not re-derived). 03-operation-lifecycle.md:557 (move send step) and 03:353 (raw pay) run the cap check on the quote and then issue the lnv2 send. 07-security-requirements.md:164 (SEC-7) distinguishes the wallet's amount caps from the protocol schedule limits. The SDK's send fetches routing_info again and builds the outgoing contract from that response, so a gateway can quote within the wallet cap and then raise its fee within FMI-19's protocol envelope; nothing binds the funded contract's fee to the admitted cap.
Fix: require the funded outgoing contract's fee (and the federation's send quote on it) to be validated against the admitted cap BEFORE funding — pass the quoted fee as the limit to the send, or read the contract the send will fund and refuse when over; class Permanent with a named message. Add an adversarial scenario: gateway raises its fee between quote and send; the wallet funds nothing.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
PROMOTED to blocker (Astra, Sol; Fable/Opus major): a conforming-looking implementation funds above the user's admitted cap. Verified by all four against the pinned SDK (72b1e5be) and v0.12.1: send re-reads routing_info (lib.rs ~578) and funds send_fee.add_to(amount) at the terms it reads then; send_with_terms (9120506f70d, 2026-09-09) exists on upstream master only, in no tag. Corrected fix: the spec cannot command an SDK method; it requires the PROPERTY — the outgoing contract funded by the send MUST use routing terms no worse than those admitted, and when the terms changed no funding may occur. Owner: OPS-29 (the cap rule; Astra) or FMI-17 (Sol) — pick one; OPS-17 (pay) and OPS-26 (move send) cite it, SEC-7 cites it as the send-side twin of OPS-23/SEC-8. Class: NOT a blanket Permanent — a terms change is transient; use Retryable with a re-quote, consistent with OPS-26's total-over-cap Retryable, and preserve raw Pay's and the move send-leg's existing terminal semantics (Opus, Astra, Sol). ADR-0030:62-65 records this residual as accepted for the break-glass ('the cap bounds what the wallet knowingly agrees to, not what such a gateway does afterwards') — amend it explicitly or narrow it to unvetted gateways. Scenario here: a gateway raises its fee between quote and send; the wallet funds nothing; mark it as one the reference implementation fails until the SDK exposes terms-bound sends (a code-repo finding, not a spec softening).

title: Delivered net omits the mint output fee FMI-15 admits; CNF-11 demands an exact credit with no fee fixture
description:
MAJOR, Astra, PLAUSIBLE. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:297 defines delivered net as invoice - receive_quote, what the destination is actually credited; 03:454 (OPS-44) sizes and enforces the cap on that arithmetic. 02-fedimint-integration.md:218 (FMI-15) admits the federation's mint output fee on the claim, which the lnv2 receive quote does not include. So the computed delivered net can exceed the real credit. 10-conformance-checklist.md:79 (CNF-10) tolerates a bounded shortfall while 10:87 (CNF-11) requires B to rise by exactly the amount, under an environment (10:20-27) that fixes no fee schedule.
Fix: define requested, quoted and credited amounts once and use the right one in each rule (cap enforcement on the quoted delivered net is fine if stated; balance assertions on the credited amount); rewrite CNF-11's assertion as a bound, or fix the fixture's fees so exactly is true, and say so.
close_reason: Merged into spec-1nc (one fee/credit arithmetic change, one owner) on all four reviewers' recommendation.

title: Attempt-fence outcome class drifts: OPS-10/OPS-13 say Retryable, STO-9/OPS-43 say Permanent, OPS-4 forbids Failed
description:
MAJOR, Fable, verified by quote. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:162-164 (OPS-10): every durable writer is attempt-fenced: a write by a stale attempt writes nothing, and a drive treats that as Retryable; 03:199-201 (OPS-13) the same for every artifact write. 05-persistence.md:186-190 (STO-9): the admission insert, a plain status write and the retryable reset report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error; 03:256-257 (OPS-43): the reset requires the current Executing attempt, else Permanent. 03:54-58 (OPS-4): a journal failure MUST NOT produce a Failed intent. The class an implementer records, and the ledger error string (STO-35), differ by which rule is followed.
Fix: STO-9 owns it — a fenced write writes nothing and reports not-applied; a drive treats not-applied as Retryable and terminalizes nothing — and OPS-10, OPS-13, OPS-43 cite it.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Opus: reconcilable as written; Fable, Astra: no behavioural divergence; Sol: real but the OPS-4 appeal is misattributed). STO-9 already splits fenced writes into two groups (05:186-190): the admission insert, plain status write and retryable reset 'report a differing stored attempt as a Permanent error' (a STORAGE error class, STO-7), and 'every other fenced write … writes nothing and reports that it did not apply', which is what OPS-10/OPS-13's Retryable refers to. OPS-4 rules the first group ('terminalizes nothing … MUST NOT produce a Failed intent'). Nothing reaches the ledger error. Residual: 'Permanent' names both a storage error class and a perform outcome, and OPS-43's 'else Permanent' reads as the latter. Fix: a wording change in STO-9 — 'a stale-attempt refusal, never a perform outcome' — and OPS-43 cites it. Do NOT re-class the reset (STO-8 relies on 'Permanent on a failed guard').

title: FMI-40 private-network gateway allowance has no home: add a walletd.toml key / standalone flag, default off
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Opus, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:138-152 (FMI-40): MUST treat as unavailable — without connecting — a loopback, RFC 1918 or unique-local host; a host MAY offer an explicit configuration that permits private-network gateways — a test environment's gateways are on loopback — and that configuration MUST default to off. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:19-24 (HST-2) and 08:40-50 (HST-3, five keys, MUST reject any other) leave no place for it. 10:20-27 puts every conformance gateway on a vetted list; 07:218-219 (SEC-18) says the build a scenario runs on is the implementation's own. On a release build every local harness gateway is unavailable and no money scenario can pass.
Fix: a sixth HST-3 key (and the standalone flag in HST-10), default off, named in FMI-40; or state in chapter 10's environment that gateways are reachable at public addresses.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor and RECAST (Astra, Sol: FMI-40 says a host 'MAY offer' the configuration, and chapter 10 does not require loopback gateways, so no contradiction exists and 'no money scenario can pass' was an unstated harness assumption; Fable, Opus kept major on the practical ground that every local harness is loopback). Recast: an optional feature decision. If the product offers private-network gateways, the switch needs a home — a named HST-3 key (e.g. allow_private_gateways, default off), the standalone flag in the CLI grammar (spec-ee9), FMI-40 naming the owner and keeping 'MUST NOT affect the link-local and metadata rule'; its scope must match whatever spec-22p decides (gateways only, or every egress class). Fold the decision into spec-22p's list; nothing else to do here until it is taken.

title: Discovery sources cannot be configured: FMI-28's {base} comes from nowhere; STO-15 has a Nostr source ALC-28 never collects
description:
MAJOR, Opus, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:433-434 (FMI-28): GET {base}/federations — nothing says where {base} comes from or how many Observer sources exist. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:396 (ALC-28) collects from Observer, Manual; what a Manual source is and where its invites come from is unstated. 05-persistence.md:298 (STO-15) has DiscoverySource in {Observer, Nostr, Manual} — Nostr is collected by nothing. HST-3 is closed at five keys, the Policy row (STO-13, 05:249-268) has no source field, HST-2 is complete. CNF-17 and CNF-20 nonetheless require a discovery source announcing a federation.
Fix: a requirement (HST-3 key or Policy fields) for the Observer base URL(s) and the Manual source's input, with defaults, the source label used in discover:<label> keys (STO-6) and the collection order; reconcile the source enum (drop Nostr or specify it).

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; one harmful clause removed: do NOT drop Nostr — DiscoverySource is persisted (CandidateRecord.source, Discover.source; STO-15, STO-29), OVR-14 lets a persisted type change only by gaining fields, and DOM-12 / FMI-43 already state 'No requirement in this set produces a Nostr candidate' — keep it as dormant vocabulary. Hidden product decision (Opus): whether a DEFAULT Observer base (e.g. observer.fedimint.org/api) is enabled — ADR-0019 leaves 'consume the Observer API as a bootstrap prior vs run our own collection' open; chapter 11 unless an owner decides. Design decisions the agent takes: HST-3 keys vs Policy fields (CONTEXT.md Policy reserves host/deployment concerns like paths and ports for the host, which argues HST-3; OVR-8/DOM-15 put discovery caps in Policy, which argues Policy — choose and say why); the <label> values and indices of discover:<label>[:<index>]:<nonce> (STO-6); the Manual source's input; collection order; duplicate announcements and competing invites. Edit HST-3's 'five keys' sentence in the same change as any other new key (spec-iym, spec-iq9). spec-22p and spec-ee9 depend on this.

title: Standing-instruction acknowledgement is 'decided' (ch. 11, ADR-0014) but no requirement records or gates on it
description:
MAJOR, Opus + Astra + Sol. 11-open-questions.md:18-25 (question 1): that acknowledgement is decided and not in question. docs/adr/0014:10-13: an explicit, plain-language, gating acknowledgement BEFORE any funds are received; CONTEXT.md:281-289 calls it recorded. The complete API table (04:100), the fresh-admission checks (03:77) and the complete journal tag table (05:77) supply no acceptance operation, durable acknowledgement or enforcement check. Whether a headless daemon may run the allocator or accept a receive without it is unstated; on walletd the engine is ON with no compliant way to ship it off (HST-6 starts the scheduler, ALC-42 makes a stopped scheduler fatal, STO-13 has no off switch).
Fix: an owned requirement (OVR/STO) defining the acknowledgement's durable representation, acceptance surface, scope and which inbound operations are refused before it — or state that the daemon's seeded policy row IS the acknowledgement; reword question 1 to the Android onboarding flow only.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; severity split (Sol: blocker — every surface that could represent the acknowledgement is closed; others major). Correction (Astra, Sol): the seeded policy row CANNOT be the acknowledgement — it is created automatically by init, and ADR-0014 requires an 'explicit, plain-language, gating acknowledgement BEFORE any funds are received'; do not replace consent with initialization, and do not fabricate acceptance on migration. Lead with the stronger finding: for walletd the set already answers open question 1 (HST-6 starts the scheduler unconditionally, ALC-42 makes a stopped one fatal, STO-13 has no off switch), contrary to 'the set is silent until answered'. Fix: a domain owner (DOM-22, next free DOM, or OVR-15) for the acknowledgement state and gate — content, durable representation (a STO row), acceptance surface (API + CLI), which inbound operations OPS-5 refuses before it, behaviour on fresh stores, existing stores, recovery and restart, per host — and reword question 1 to the presentation/default-on choice only. Do not narrow question 1 to Android without spec-11k's scope decision.

title: Android host is in scope by prose (OVR-1, executive summary, ADR-0003/0011/0031) and specified nowhere in chapter 08
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Opus + Sol. 00-overview.md:20-26 (OVR-1) says chapter 08 owns the hosts and frontends a compliant wallet provides; executive-summary.md:18-22 and CONTEXT.md:56-60, 373-376 describe an Android app with silent backup; ADR-0003 (Block Store recovery), ADR-0011 (Keystore, biometric-to-send), ADR-0031 (in-process engine, WorkManager wakes; the watchdog's restart model needs an Android answer) are accepted. Chapter 08 specifies walletd, standalone, the CLI and the sidecar only.
Fix: either state in OVR-1 that Android is out of this version's compliance scope (and mark the ADRs' Android clauses as pending a host chapter), or write the host contract: key storage, backup/recovery, lifecycle and wake scheduling, watchdog behaviour, authentication gates, frontend/engine boundary, with scenarios.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Opus, Fable: a scope statement; OVR-1 already makes chapter 08 the complete host list, so no Android obligation exists and no implementation is non-compliant for lacking one). But option 1 is NOT a bead-sized edit either (Astra, Sol): ADR-0032:17 names 'the hosts (a daemon, an Android app, a browser sidecar, wasm where named)', so removing Android from the compliance scope is a new ADR superseding the Android portions of ADR-0003/0011/0031, plus edits to OVR-1, the executive summary and the CONTEXT.md Host / Silent backup entries. Keeping it means HST-34+ (next free HST) host requirements — observable key protection, authentication gates, backup/recovery, lifecycle and wakes, restart/failure, engine ownership — without JNI/WorkManager mechanism, plus scenarios. Actionable now: the chapter-11 entry naming the scope decision. Coordinate with spec-dn8 (the acknowledgement's home) and spec-iym (Keystore is a second key-source mechanism).

title: Evacuation hop routing is owned by the glossary and ADR-0029 only; no FMI/OPS rule, no deadline, no hop scenario
description:
MAJOR, 4/4 reviewers, verified. CONTEXT.md:223-241 (Shared route / Hop) states the loop normatively: ranked together, cheapest composed cost among different-node combinations first, the next tried when the first sizes to nothing viable, a failed hop sets aside that node pair. docs/adr/0029:50-84 gives the composed-cost formula, tie-break (lower receive fee, then the ordered pair of URLs) and per-attempt deadline — by function name (quote_fresh_send_required_cost, FreshMoveCost::total_fee), which fails the refactor test. 00-overview.md:104-108 (OVR-13) and 02:197-201 (FMI-14) say in ADR-0029's order; 03:435-440 (OPS-21) snapshots one gateway fee per leg without saying how the two gateways are chosen; 02:282-297 (FMI-22) bounds the fallback scan at 10 s and names no bound for the class scan. Chapter 10 cites OVR-13 zero times: the environment (10:20-27) always has a shared gateway G, CNF-14 uses it, CNF-53 is one break-glass gateway — a shared-route-only implementation passes.
Fix: FMI-44 (or extend FMI-14): candidate set = validated destination list x validated source list on distinct lightning_public_key; order by composed cost at the ask (ALC-13's formula), ties by lower receive fee then URL pair; next combination on an empty sizing result; one per-attempt deadline named in FMI-22; what journaled as truncated writes. CONTEXT.md and ADR-0029 cite it. Add a CNF with disjoint vetted lists on distinct Lightning nodes asserting route identities, both fee legs, committed-route replay and fallback after a failed performer.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; the fix needs more decisions named. (1) The proposed cost formula was WRONG (Astra): ADR-0029:54 requires the FULL route cost including the federation quotes on the contracts gross-up implies (FMI-18/OPS-44), not ALC-13's planning model — rank by the actual composed cost, then the accepted tie-breaks. (2) The shared class's own candidate loop for an EVACUATION (amount sized, not final; 'try a candidate, size it, on nothing viable try the next, then the next class') — FMI-14's steps are written for a final amount. (3) The per-attempt deadline must be a named constant in FMI-22, because 'inside perform_timeout' is undefined when the timeout is 0 (Opus); its relation to the perform budget; what a truncated search writes to the ledger row (a warning, an error text, nothing). (4) Which route's samples become the OPS-31 marker when both classes refuse (decides ALC-23 qualification). (5) A hop hint cannot be carried: Evacuate has one gateway? field (DOM-7) while the glossary says a hop hint is two identities — say so. (6) Cache-loss replay for hops: in STO-33 gateway names the gateway for THAT leg, so OPS-20 must reconstruct destination and source roles explicitly, never an undifferentiated newest gateway. (7) Set-aside (FMI-42) and the prohibition on switching after commitment. (8) The attempt-level sense of 'serves' ('serves this attempt') lives here (spec-hrb). Correct executive-summary.md:64-65, which says an ordinary move hops. FMI-44 only if no earlier FMI lands first. The hop CNF lands HERE: disjoint vetted lists on distinct Lightning nodes, cache loss both before and after the send record exists, route identities, both fee legs, fallback after a failed performer. Depends on spec-1nc (the composed cost uses the settled amount contract).

title: ALC-39 sleeps on meta_module_expiry_secs, which FMI-3 and FMI-26 say is not an input
description:
MAJOR, 4/4 reviewers, verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:615-617 (ALC-39): the expiry deadlines are, per probed federation, only the corroborated config_expiry_secs and meta_module_expiry_secs (FMI-26). 02-fedimint-integration.md:405-406 (FMI-26): the meta module's consensus value is not an input (FMI-3); 02:32 (FMI-3): the meta module is not consumed. Neither name is defined anywhere, and the config expiry is trusted, not corroborated, in FMI-26's own taxonomy.
Fix: restate ALC-39 in FMI-26's vocabulary (the at-join config federation_expiry_timestamp, and a /status shutdown corroborated by f+1 peers, when in the future) and drop the meta-module deadline; or define the signal in FMI-26 and withdraw the not-consumed sentences.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; option 1 corrected (Opus, Astra, Sol): the /status scheduled_shutdown carries a SESSION INDEX ('whatever session index it names', FMI-26:416-417), not a time, and a corroborated signal schedules at once — it cannot be a sleep deadline, and ALC-39 already excludes 'the /status flag'. The deadline set is therefore exactly the at-join config federation_expiry_timestamp (FMI-26), when in the future; the override-meta wake stays in ALC-39's last sentence as a wake, never a deadline. Remove meta_module_expiry_secs and the undefined config_expiry_secs name. Owner ALC-39.

title: FMI-19 component-wise fee limit has no wallet-side enforcer; OPS-21 and ADR-0029 say the protocol refuses lexicographically
description:
MAJOR, Opus + Sol, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:273-280 (FMI-19): a schedule above the limit MUST be refused; above is component-wise ... never a lexicographic comparison; this is an admission filter on the posted schedule; the class each refusal takes is FMI-16's and FMI-17's. 03:439-440 (OPS-21): warning, never refusing, on a schedule outside FMI-19's limits (the protocol refuses at the send). docs/adr/0029:26-29: the SDK's limits bound each leg's BASE but not the ppm because PaymentFee compares lexicographically. FMI-17 classes gateway fee over limit as a protocol refusal. By the ADR the protocol does NOT refuse a base-under, ppm-over schedule, so OPS-21's parenthetical is false and no rule tells the wallet to apply the check, where, or with what class.
Fix: make FMI-19 a wallet-side check with a stated point (at selection and before the lnv2 receive/send call) and class (Retryable for receive per FMI-16, Permanent for send per FMI-17); correct OPS-21; amend the ADR-0029 note to cite FMI-19 as the resulting decision.
close_reason: Premise false (Opus; re-verified): the public SDK compares fee limits component-wise since v0.12.0 (commit d5febdf9d37, 2026-07-30, fedimint-lnv2-common gateway_api.rs is_within), applied on send and receive. OPS-21's '(the protocol refuses at the send)' is therefore true and SEC-7 is consistent with it; a wallet-side second enforcer would violate one-owner-per-rule. Only ADR-0029:26-29's lexicographic note is stale, and spec-y0b owns that amendment.

title: ADR-0030 §4 (and ADR-0022 backup, ADR-0003) contradict newer requirements; README:43 makes the ADR win
description:
MAJOR, Opus + Sol + Fable, verified. docs/adr/0030:47-49: after cache loss a send-required move's committed gateway is not recoverable from the op-log; such a re-drive resolves afresh. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:416-421 (OPS-20): Committed -> the route MUST replay as recorded, from the cache and, after cache loss, from the gateway ... the committed leg's metadata carries (STO-33, 05:558-559); FMI-14 cites ADR-0030 §4 as the owner of committed-route replay. README.md:43: ADRs are canonical where they conflict with older prose — so a reviewer could hold an implementation to the ADR. Same staleness: docs/adr/0022:70-73 (backup must include in-flight move state) vs STO-28 / ADR-0025 (never the local stores) and FMI-32; docs/adr/0003:9 (federation IDs) vs invite codes; ADR-0029:26-29 lexicographic note vs FMI-19.
Fix: amendment notes on ADR-0030 §4 (superseded by STO-33 gateway/send_gateway, with OPS-20's legacy exception), ADR-0022 (backup unit is ADR-0025's) and ADR-0029; narrow README:43 to: an ADR is canonical for the decision and what was rejected; the requirement owns the current mechanism and wins where it is newer.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
PARTIAL (all four): the README:43 claim was a misreading — it says 'Canonical where they conflict with OLDER prose', so OPS-20/STO-33 (newer) already win over ADR-0030 and no compliant implementation follows the ADR; the real gap is that a reviewer cannot tell which is older without git, and that FMI-14 cites ADR-0030 §4 as the OWNER of committed-route replay. Do not introduce a general 'newer prose wins' rule (Astra: it would let a behavioural change evade ADR review); narrow README:43 to 'canonical for the decision and what was rejected; the requirement owns the current mechanism', and add dated amendment notes (precedent: ADR-0004 'as amended', ADR-0028): ADR-0030 §4 → OPS-20/STO-33 with the legacy-metadata exception; ADR-0022:70-73 → ADR-0025/STO-28/SEC-24; ADR-0029:26-29 (lexicographic fee note — stale against both FMI-19 and the SDK since v0.12.0; absorbed from the closed spec-ezl) and ADR-0029's hop text → FMI-44 once spec-bqv lands. ADR-0003's 'federation IDs' is already annotated by ADR-0025 §1 — drop that item. ADRs are not gated by the codebase-reference ratchet (check_ids.py gates NN-*.md, CONTEXT.md, executive-summary.md only), so the function names in ADR-0029/0030 are a refactor-test smell, not a gate failure. Depends on spec-bqv for the hop note.

title: Probe leg fee cap default is stated three incompatible ways (FMI-34 10 sats, STO-13 max_fee 200 sats, STO-26 10_000 msat)
description:
MAJOR, Opus, verified. 02-fedimint-integration.md:461-462 (FMI-34): leg fee cap max_fee (default 10 sats per leg in the standalone verb). 05-persistence.md:257 (STO-13): seeded max_fee 200_000 msat. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:47-52 (ALC-3): every planning and probing path MUST run under the stored Policy ... its probe amount and leg fee cap (max_fee); the verdict is computed under the stored max_fee. 05:470-471 (STO-26): default-qualifying means ok && amount_msat >= 20_000 && leg_fee_cap_msat <= 10_000 — under the stored default no attempt is ever default-qualifying, so pruning silently diverges from the verdict (ALC-25) and the budget (ALC-26). HST-10 lists no probe flag.
Fix: (a) delete default 10 sats from FMI-34 and key STO-26's keep rule to the stored probe_amount / max_fee; or (b) a dedicated Policy field for the leg cap with its default, cited by ALC-3, ALC-25, ALC-26, STO-26. Either way HST-10 lists any standalone probe flag. Also reconcile FMI-34's per-leg cap with ALC-27's leg-OUT cap min(leg_cap, delivered_in - out_net) (06:371-374).

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; narrowed. Two incompatible defaults, not three (Sol, Astra): FMI-34's 10 sats vs STO-13's stored max_fee 200 sats under ALC-3. STO-26's leg_fee_cap_msat <= 10_000 is a RETENTION category, not a default; and the retention analysis was overstated (Astra): STO-26 first keeps every attempt within 7 days plus the newest and newest-ok per source, so Expired/NeverProbed stay correct; the effect is limited to which attempts survive beyond seven days. The ALC-27 leg-OUT min(...) sentence is NOT a contradiction (Opus, Astra, Sol): a stricter OUT cap satisfies the per-leg maximum; drop it. Fix: delete 'default 10 sats' from FMI-34 and cite STO-13; reconcile STO-26's default-qualifying rule with the stored probe_amount/max_fee at the time of the write — do not key pruning to the CURRENT policy (a later edit would reinterpret history — Sol); any standalone probe flag lands in API-44 (spec-ee9). A dedicated leg-cap Policy field is a separate product decision. Owners FMI-34, STO-26.

title: ALC-16 rank term '+50 if a peg-out fee is quotable' has no producer; ALC-49 forbids the read and FMI-3 the module
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Opus. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:247-248 (ALC-16): min(threshold, guardian_count) x 100, + 50 if a peg-out fee is quotable, - latency_ms / 10. 01:113-116 (DOM-14) and 06:705-711 (ALC-49): the light probe is one threshold read, one pass over the vetted list and one read of the shutdown signals; a second light probe in the same cycle is not permitted. 02:29-30 (FMI-3): the wallet module is exposed only so the config decodes and the network can be read. Rank decides auto-designation (DOM-4), wire-visible in /v1/status (spending_fed, standby_fed), so two compliant implementations designate differently.
Fix: delete the + 50 term, or specify the read (protocol request, amount/address, success criterion) and schedule it in ALC-15 / ALC-49, amending FMI-3.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four. Delete the '+ 50' term (Fable, Sol): a peg-out fee has no meaning in a wallet that MUST NOT peg in or out (FMI-3, OVR-11, ADR-0004); FMI-3's 'only' is the prohibition (ALC-49 merely enumerates the light probe's reads — Opus). Astra notes ADR-0019 accepted the ranking: amend that ADR's ranking clause in the same change. Rank changes for the existing implementation are a code-repo hand-off. Owner ALC-16.

title: ALC-28 step 2 decides on 'agent-created', a fact no row carries, and turns a user-joined federation without a row into AutoJoined
description:
MAJOR, Fable, verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:399-402 (ALC-28 step 2): a joined federation whose row is Discovered/Rejected and whose registry entry is agent-created becomes AutoJoined/Passed; a joined federation with no row gets one from its joined invite (source: Manual, AutoJoined, Passed). 05-persistence.md:83 (STO-5): FederationInfo {invite, db_prefix, joined_at} — no actor. 03:605-609 (OPS-42): a user join marks a candidate UserApproved only from a state that is neither AutoJoined nor already UserApproved; it does not say a row is created when none exists. 07:198-202 (SEC-16): a user's own join is trusted as the user's decision. So agent-created is underivable, and a hand-joined federation with no candidate row becomes probe-gated AutoJoined, unfundable until approve — against SEC-16.
Fix: OPS-42 creates a UserApproved row (source: Manual) when none exists; ALC-28 step 2 decides agent-created by the presence of an agent join:<fed>:<nonce> ledger row, or FederationInfo gains an actor field under STO-30. Also give FederationInfo's fields types (FMI-20 contemplates an invite that does not parse).

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED (Fable, Sol; Opus/Astra PARTIAL). Corrections: ALC-37 (06:390-391) 'a user join writes it only when no AutoJoined row already exists' already implies creation when no row exists, so the no-row case arises mainly from a crash between the registry write and the candidate write; OPS-42's 'mark the candidate' is still ambiguous and must say it creates the row (STO-26's recovery template {source: Manual, structural: Passed, state: UserApproved} fixes the fields), in the join's registry transaction. Worse than stated (Fable): DOM-3/ALC-37 probe-gate ANY joined federation without a UserApproved row, so if the row is not created the conformance environment's own A and B are probe-gated and CNF-13 refuses NotProbed — the set only works if the row exists. Simplest fix, no provenance needed (Fable): ALC-28 step 2 treats a joined federation whose row is absent or not UserApproved as agent-joined (fail-closed, exactly ALC-37's rule for an unreadable row) and approve releases it; do NOT infer 'agent-created' from the join:<fed>:<nonce> ledger row (best-effort under OVR-4, may be absent — Astra, Opus) and do not add an actor field. If provenance is truly needed it goes in FederationInfo under STO-30 with a legacy default that never silently becomes user approval. FederationInfo's field types move to the new persisted-types bead.

title: Unaffordable route hint: CONTEXT.md re-resolves it, FMI-14 step 2 / OPS-22 terminalize Permanent
description:
MAJOR, Fable, verified. CONTEXT.md:197-207 (Route hint): kept only while it holds, otherwise re-resolved under the same fee cap ... so a holding hint can still prove unaffordable and be re-resolved. 02-fedimint-integration.md:186 (FMI-14 step 2): the action's route hint, if it still holds (FMI-13) — taken; step 3's cheapest fitting candidate is reached only when the hint does not hold. 03:507-511 (OPS-22): receive-leg cap check ... over is persisted first, then Retryable for Evacuate, Permanent otherwise. A funding Move with a holding hint whose quote rose over the cap is Permanent; the same move without a hint is Retryable and re-priced (FMI-14 step 3, 02:188-191). Different terminals for the same economic state, observable on the ledger; the glossary owns behaviour nothing states.
Fix: add to FMI-14 step 2: a holding hint whose receive quote at the amount exceeds the cap is discarded and step 3 runs; or delete the glossary clause and let OPS-22's Permanent stand. CONTEXT.md cites the owner.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four (Opus: borderline minor — only the glossary disagrees; the requirements are consistent with each other). Take option A (Fable, Sol: 'a hint, never a constraint' is the stronger existing decision): FMI-14 step 2 says a holding hint whose route proves unaffordable at the amount is discarded and step 3 runs; OPS-22 terminalizes only after that resolution fails. Correction (Astra): checking the destination receive quote alone is insufficient — a hint can pass it and fail the combined send/receive check or size to nothing; define the fallback for the complete UNCOMMITTED hinted route after pricing/sizing, and keep OPS-20/FMI-23's committed-route rules untouched. Only allocator funding Moves carry a hint (API-18/API-31 put no gateway on the wire; probe legs carry none) — worth saying. Absorb DEF-5 (09:49, 'the whole candidate set, never by a candidate's position') here: replace its duplicate selection rule with citations that preserve the hint and bounded-scan exceptions. CONTEXT.md Route hint cites FMI-14.

title: Policy validity predicate is two lines (ALC-7, ALC-20); DOM-15 / API-20 require rejecting any invalid policy naming the field
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Astra + Sol. 01-domain-model.md:120-123 (DOM-15): MUST validate the stored row, MUST refuse to run under an invalid one, MUST reject an edit that would store one (API-20); 04-api-contract.md:289-290 (API-20): 422 policy_invalid naming the field. Owners of validity: 06:126-127 (ALC-7) max_fee_bps_of_move 0 or above 10 000; 06:294-295 (ALC-20) a bps above 10 000 or the pair (0, 0). Nothing else: min_interval_secs > base_interval_secs makes ALC-38's at most the base / at least the minimum (06:566) and ALC-39's clamp (06:608) undefined; probe_min_successes = 0, spending_target > per_fed_cap, probe_ttl_secs > 604 800 (silently ineffective under STO-26's constant window) are all accepted. Two implementations accept different PUT /v1/policy bodies; CNF-33 / CNF-26 cannot decide it.
Fix: one requirement with the exhaustive predicate — per-field ranges and the relational constraints — deterministic first-error ordering for the named field, and the sentence that no other check is permitted; distinguish legal-but-ineffective values from invalid ones.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; not self-contained. Owner: ALC-54 (next free ALC) holds the exhaustive predicate; ALC-7 and ALC-20 keep owning their two ranges and are cited; DOM-15, API-20, HST-6/STO-13's start-time validation and the standalone overrides (ALC-3) all reference ALC-54. Verified undefined: min_interval_secs > base_interval_secs (ALC-39's clamp; Rust's Ord::clamp panics); ALC-52's max(min_successes - 1, 1) at 0 unless saturating; base_interval_secs = 0 (busy loop); probe_amount < 5 000 msat (can never mint, FMI-16); discover_pass_deadline_secs = 0. The other examples are DECISIONS, not automatically invalid (Astra, Sol): spending_target > per_fed_cap, probe_min_successes = 0, probe_ttl_secs > 604 800 (ALC-25 explicitly reads 'the retained history, which STO-26 prunes') may be legal-but-ineffective — the predicate must say which, and end with 'all other correctly typed values are legal'. Deterministic first-error ordering for the named field; decoding errors distinct from semantic invalidity. Upgrade hazard (Opus): DOM-15/STO-13 make a resident host refuse to start on an invalid stored row, so tightening the predicate can brick an existing store — choose a disposition (refuse naming the field, or grandfather + warn) and add the code-repo hand-off. Depends on spec-9iq if it adds a policy field.

title: ALC-17's Unhealthy evacuation branch is unreachable: the snapshot only holds federations whose light probe succeeded
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:29-32 (ALC-1): the snapshot carries the joined, open federations whose light probe succeeded (FMI-25) ... its healthy flag — FMI-25's quorum_live, the threshold read that succeeded. 02-fedimint-integration.md:395-397 (FMI-25): a federation whose light probe errors is dropped from the snapshot with a warning and is therefore neither scored nor evacuated that cycle. 06:260-261 (ALC-17): Unhealthy when it is not healthy. healthy is always true for a snapshot member, so the branch has no constructible input and CONTEXT.md:80-88's backstop for unplanned degradation is not delivered.
Fix: keep a bounded negative liveness verdict in the snapshot (a threshold read that answered below quorum, distinct from an indeterminate transport error), or remove Unhealthy from ALC-17 and the glossary's claim.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Fable, Opus: dead branch, no divergence). Option 1 is flawed (Fable, Opus, Astra): a federation whose threshold read fails or answers below quorum cannot sign the lnv2 send an evacuation needs, so a negative-liveness Evacuate would be Retryable forever; and 'a threshold read that answered below quorum' is not a usable observation (a successful threshold read has reached its threshold). Whether unplanned degradation should evacuate at all is a product decision (Astra, Sol) → chapter 11. Interim fix: delete the Unhealthy branch from ALC-17, keep Unhealthy as ReasonCode vocabulary (ALC-48's refuse:unhealthy:<fed>:<occurrence> row uses it), and change ALC-48's key-shape sentence ('the prefix is what tells this row from ALC-17's no-destination refusal') with it; correct CONTEXT.md:87-88's 'backstop for unplanned degradation' to what is delivered (an Unhealthy refusal row, no evacuation).

title: OPS-11 / ALC-53 use 'world generation', 'plan authority' and 'balance authority', none defined; CONTEXT.md knows three generations only
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:167-169 (OPS-11): the batch MUST be refused whole on a stale policy generation (ALC-41), a changed world generation, an invalid plan or balance-facts authority, or more than one occurrence. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:773-775 (ALC-53): the world generation, the plan authority, the balance authority. CONTEXT.md:325-330 (Generation) defines a balance generation per federation, a membership generation and a policy generation, with owners OPS-13, OPS-6, ALC-41. Nothing defines issuance, content, invalidation or equivalence of the other three, so whole-batch acceptance cannot be implemented or reviewed independently.
Fix: define each (world generation = the pair of membership and balance generations? plan authority = the eligibility snapshot's generations? balance authority = the sampled balance facts' generations?) with every state change that invalidates it — or replace the three words with explicit comparisons against the defined counters and balance facts.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four. Corrected fix (all four: replace, don't define; no lease/token machinery, which would fail the refactor test): OPS-11 enumerates the observable comparisons whose change rejects the batch whole — the policy generation (ALC-41), the membership generation (OPS-6: every admission advances it 'so that no allocator plan computed over the world before this admission can commit'), the per-federation balance generations (OPS-13; ALC-35 'valid only with the balance generation that authorized it'), the sampled balance facts, and OPS-41's fence (no plan or balance facts issued during a raw terminal write or membership change) — and says how decisions accepted within the same batch interact with advancing generations. ALC-53, ALC-34 (06:530-531), ALC-38 step 9 and the glossary cite it; ALC-38 step 5's 'authorize planning' is the OPS-41 fence, not one of these. Also decide OPS-39's 'conflict — an admission racing a membership change (OPS-41)' (the review's minor): a fresh-admission guard or plan invalidation only, and make owner and mapping agree. Add a race scenario: which intervening change rejects the batch and which drops one decision. 'trusted' and 'probed' are the same class of defect and now have their own bead.

title: Journal key: STO-1 prefixes every key with 0x00, STO-5 says [tag] ++ id_bytes, STO-18 requires an exactly nine-byte ledger tail
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. 05-persistence.md:16-18 (STO-1): inside journal.db every journal key is prefixed 0x00, and a key outside that prefix is not part of the journal. 05:55 (STO-5): every journal key is [tag] ++ id_bytes, the ledger key 0x05 ++ be64(seq). 05:388-395 (STO-18): the tail is the lexicographically greatest 0x05 key, which MUST be a canonical nine-byte key; a tail key that is not exactly nine bytes is the fence. Either 0x00 is an outer namespace the nine bytes sit under (then STO-5's key is the logical key and the raw key is ten bytes, and every scan/prefix rule must say which), or the ledger key is nine bytes and STO-1 is wrong. Two implementations write mutually unreadable stores.
