Fix: state the raw byte sequence once in STO-5 (e.g. 0x00 ++ tag ++ id_bytes, with lengths), distinguish namespace prefix from logical key wherever a length or lexicographic rule appears (STO-18, STO-10 index keys), and correct the nine-byte sentences.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four (severity split: Opus minor, Fable/Astra major, Sol blocker). Reconcilable reading (Opus, Astra): STO-1's 0x00 is a namespace ('a key outside that prefix is not part of the journal'; STO-3 uses the same pattern for client.db, and the withdrawn DEF-24 / CNF-51 read it so), STO-5's [tag] ++ id_bytes is the LOGICAL key within it, and the raw key is 0x00 ++ logical. The defect is that 'journal key' names both, so STO-18's 'not exactly nine bytes' is literally false of raw bytes. Fix, one sentence in STO-5: keys and lengths in this chapter are logical keys under STO-1's 0x00 namespace; the raw ledger key is 00 || 05 || be64(seq), ten bytes; then check every scan, index and canonical-length statement (STO-1/10/18/19/20/22/24/25) says which view it means. Do NOT change any byte or replace nine with ten (OVR-14). The raw-byte truth is a fact about existing stores, not a choice — if any doubt remains, the code repository's persistence layer is the input.

title: 'Serves' is defined in CONTEXT.md as including 'performs', but FMI-11 / FMI-13 use it for a decoded RoutingInfo before any operation
description:
MAJOR, Sol, verified. CONTEXT.md:143-153 (Serves): a gateway serves when it is on the vetted list, validates, an economically viable amount can be sized over it, AND it performs — completes every leg it quoted. 02-fedimint-integration.md:131 (FMI-11): a decoded RoutingInfo means the gateway serves that federation; FMI-13 (02:166-173) uses serves before sizing or performance; ALC eligibility (06:235-245) asks whether a gateway serves. A pre-operation routing predicate thus depends circularly on an operation having completed.
Fix: three terms — validates (FMI-11's decoded RoutingInfo), is viable for an amount (sizing), performed (completed the quoted legs) — reserve serves for exactly one stage, and update every use in CONTEXT.md, FMI-11, FMI-13, FMI-14, ALC-5, ALC-13.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Fable, Opus: FMI-11 and FMI-13 define their own sense explicitly, so an implementer of FMI-11..14 / ALC-13/15/27/32 has nothing to guess; the circularity lives in CONTEXT.md, whose entry is vocabulary). Real residuals: the glossary disagrees with its owner; FMI-42 amends FMI-13's definition from outside it ('A set-aside gateway does not serve'); and ADR-0029's attempt-level sense ('does not serve THIS attempt', quoted by FMI-14:198 and OVR-13) is a third sense that is load-bearing for the evacuation fall-through — that one belongs in spec-bqv's FMI-44. Lighter fix (Opus): FMI-13 owns 'serves' (validation + both-ends), set-aside folded in; the glossary cites it; the attempt-level sense gets its own phrase ('serves this attempt'), used only in the evacuation route classes. The use list in the original fix was wrong: ALC-5 does not use the word; missing are ALC-15, ALC-18, ALC-27, ALC-32, FMI-42, SEC-17, OVR-13, OPS-21, the chapter-10 environment, CNF-17/CNF-20, ADR-0029.

title: CLI argument grammar is absent: HST-10 ends its flag list in '…', API-25 enumerates verb names only, so CNF-26 cannot be judged
description:
MAJOR, Opus. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:175-181 (HST-10): the standalone-only verb shapes and flags are the set API-25 enumerates ... (--per-fed-cap, --evac-fee-*, --occurrence, …). 04-api-contract.md:341-354 (API-25 / API-26): verb names and the request fields each sends, not positional vs flag arguments, not the arguments of probe, discover, tick, status, history --fed, show <seq>, not the complete override list. 06:50 (ALC-3): HST-10 lists the flags. 10:313-335 (CNF-26) asserts each verb sends exactly the named fields; without the grammar two compliant CLIs are script-incompatible and the scenario cannot be staged uniformly.
Fix: one API-n table: every verb's positional arguments, flags, defaults and mode (client / standalone / both), including the full override flag list; HST-10 and ALC-3 cite it.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four. Corrections: the grammar is INCOMPLETE, not absent — API-27 (policy flags), API-38 (<key> --timeout), API-39 (approve <hex>, show <key>), API-40 (history filters), API-41 (--nonce/--occurrence/--fee-cap/--to/--fed, 'move --occurrence defaults to 0') and API-25's global flags exist; the new table (API-44, next free API) must absorb them by citation, never copy a default into a second normative table. Genuinely unspecified: positional vs flag arguments and shapes for pay, move, receive, direct-inflow, join, recover, probe, discover, tick, status, history --fed, show <seq>; repeatability; mutually exclusive pairs; client/standalone availability; the full override list and which Policy fields standalone tick/status may override (ALC-3, OPS-7 'MUST be validated'). The grammar is not derivable from this repository (Fable, Opus): name the input — ratify the code repository's CLI --help — so the agent does not invent one that gives the existing CLI a finding per divergence. HST-10 and ALC-3 cite API-44. Depends on spec-6w6 (adds config/flags) and the new default-fee_cap bead (the grammar states defaults it cannot invent); land after spec-9iq if it adds a probe flag.

title: OPS-5's '24 hours when no perform timeout is configured' is unreachable under HST-2's 600 s default
description:
MAJOR, Fable + Opus, verified. 03-operation-lifecycle.md:72-74 (OPS-5): probe legs are each awaited to terminal under the host's perform timeout ... or 24 hours when none is configured. 08-hosts-and-deployment.md:32 (HST-2): WALLETD_PERFORM_TIMEOUT_SECS unset or empty -> 600 s, 0 disables it; 08:159-160 (HST-9) standalone the same. None configured is 600 s, so the 24-hour bound is unreachable unless none means 0 — in which case a disabled timeout is not disabled for probe legs. Undecidable as written.
Fix: replace with: or 24 hours when the timeout is disabled (0); or delete the clause.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
DOWNGRADED to minor (Fable, Opus, Astra; Sol keeps major). Reconcilable reading: 'none is configured' = the resolved perform deadline is disabled (0). The clause is reachable only with 0 set and only for probe legs. Fix, one line in OPS-5: 'or 24 hours when the resolved perform timeout is disabled (0)'; HST-2 and HST-9 quote it. Do not delete the fallback as if it were an editorial equivalent (Astra: that changes behaviour).

title: Egress policy (FMI-40) covers gateway requests only; meta_override_url and discovery config fetches inherit nothing
description:
MAJOR, Astra, PLAUSIBLE. 02-fedimint-integration.md:138 (FMI-40): the wallet MUST NOT let a guardian direct its egress — but the address, redirect and DNS checks apply before any gateway request. 02:402 (FMI-26) reads an explicitly untrusted meta_override_url; 02:440 (FMI-28) fetches candidate configurations supplied by discovery. Neither path inherits the gateway restrictions, so a malicious guardian or poisoned feed (07:23) can induce requests to link-local / private addresses; rejecting the fetched metadata happens after connecting.
Fix: one egress rule for every untrusted endpoint the wallet contacts (gateways, override metadata, discovery sources, candidate config fetches), with explicit exceptions (the operator's own Observer base) and the redirect / DNS-rebinding rules; conformance cases per path.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; scope corrected. Strong half: the meta_override_url fetch (FMI-26) is an HTTP GET to a guardian-chosen URL — a real SSRF vector (blind: the wallet parses and never returns the body). Weak half: the discovery preview (FMI-28/ALC-28) speaks the federation transport (FMI-36: iroh, WebSocket, HTTP) to the invite's endpoints; an iroh endpoint has no host to check, and applying the gateway HTTP rules indiscriminately would break FMI-36. Extending egress to guardian endpoints also refuses every loopback conformance federation (CNF-17/CNF-20's announced C included) unless the private-network allowance (spec-iq9, now folded here) covers that class. Fix: one owner for untrusted-endpoint egress (extend FMI-40 or a new SEC-26), cited by FMI-26, FMI-28, FMI-40 and the host rules, deciding: operator-configured bases (the Observer {base}, once spec-6w6 gives it a home) vs URLs supplied by guardians or feeds; user-supplied join/recover invites are exempt (the user's decision, SEC-16); redirects, address changes at connect time, DNS rebinding; proxy behaviour under HST-2; transport-specific enforcement; which private-network exceptions apply per class, never the link-local/metadata range. Simpler product option for the meta path (Opus): stop reading the override-served expiry, which 'never schedules on its own' anyway. Conformance cases per path. Depends on spec-6w6.

title: Vetted-list reads and sequential peer /status reads have no per-request or per-cycle bound; a silent guardian stalls the cycle
description:
MAJOR, Sol, PLAUSIBLE. 02-fedimint-integration.md:112-121 (vetted list reads), 02:416-419 (peer /status reads for corroboration) and the boundary table 02:282-298 (FMI-22), which omits both. 06:561-605 (the scheduler cycle, ALC-38 / ALC-48): a non-answering guardian can therefore stall the cycle, readiness and evacuation indefinitely.
Fix: add rows to FMI-22: connect / total bounds per read, an aggregate per federation and per cycle, cancellation behaviour, and the resulting classification (no signal vs failure) for the light probe and the shutdown corroboration.

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
CONFIRMED by all four; understated: FMI-25's session_count threshold read is equally unbounded (FMI-38 bounds only waits 'while driving an intent'), and ALC-40 runs 'after every cycle' so it cannot rescue a cycle stuck before completion; HST-6 excludes status dry runs from the perform timeout. Fix: rows in FMI-22 for the per-guardian vetted-list read (FMI-10), the per-peer /status read (FMI-26), the threshold read (FMI-25) and the override-metadata fetch, plus a per-federation and per-cycle light-probe budget; the numbers are a design value the agent chooses (suggest mirroring FMI-11's 5 s connect / 10 s total per guardian); cancellation semantics; and the classification of a timeout — a timed-out guardian 'lists nothing' (FMI-10), a timed-out peer is 'no signal' (FMI-26; a timeout must never manufacture corroboration), a timed-out threshold read is a light-probe error dropped per FMI-25/ALC-48. ALC-38 cites the aggregate-cycle guarantee.

title: Conformance gaps: security MUSTs, the derivation vector, retry, watchdog, hop, killpoint 4; three scenario assertions contradict their owners
description:
MAJOR, union of all four reviewers. No scenario cites or exercises: FMI-40 (egress: a guardian-listed gateway at 169.254.169.254, an RFC 1918 address, a re-resolving DNS name), API-2 / SEC-2 (401 before 404/405, constant-time compare), SEC-14 negative case (an override-served expiry alone never schedules), FMI-7 (no known-answer vector: CNF-23 funds and recovers on the same implementation, which proves nothing about every implementation MUST reproduce exactly), OPS-10 (retry mints attempt 1 and retry:<len>:<key>:<n> metadata), ALC-40 (watchdog trips, process exits non-zero), HST-19 / HST-29 / HST-33, DOM-21 (probe/user key collision -> 409), FMI-19, FMI-38, FMI-42 (set-aside: a second selection avoids the pair), STO-18 (counter fence), ALC-30 / ALC-44 (suppression in status.suppressed), API-35 (2 MiB body), ALC-29 (auto-join at, below and above each limit), OPS-46 / STO-24 (repair strings), plus the hop evacuation and the tight-source killpoint 4 (tracked in their own beads).
Contradictory assertions: 10:284-285 (CNF-15) timestamps non-decreasing by seq vs 01:87-89 (DOM-11) timestamps carry no ordering authority and 05:362-363 (STO-16) a retry row keeps the original created_at_ms — narrow to what is observable or delete; 10:194-195 (CNF-16) it is a no-attempt that records nothing vs 06:362-367 (ALC-27), which writes the umbrella probe:<fed>:<nonce> row before the preflight — say records no attempt and changes no verdict and state the umbrella row's terminal status; CNF-24's marker assertion (own bead).
Fix: one scenario per item above, each citing the requirement and the requirement citing it back (AGENTS.md: prefer a scenario to an assertion).

## Review corrections (2026-09-23, four-model bead review: Fable, Opus, Astra, Sol)
SPLIT (all four): this bead now covers ONLY the contradictory scenario assertions, which are independent of every other fix. The coverage work (missing scenarios) is a new child titled 'Conformance coverage: the scenarios no requirement cites' and depends on the beads that own the behaviour. Corrections to the original: FMI-42 IS cited (CNF-21; what is missing is a second selection avoiding the set-aside pair) and ALC-29 IS cited (CNF-17, CNF-20; the limits are untested and cannot be until the counters are defined). Assertions to fix here: (1) CNF-15 (10:284-285) 'timestamps non-decreasing by seq' vs DOM-11 'no ordering authority' — false even for updated_at_ms within CNF-15's own session (a lower-seq row terminalizes later); narrow to what is observable (seq is the order) or delete. (2) CNF-16 (10:194-195) 'a no-attempt that records nothing' vs ALC-27 (06:361-367), which begins a session and writes the umbrella probe:<fed>:<nonce> row BEFORE the preflight — say 'records no attempt and changes no verdict', and take the umbrella row's terminal status and session cleanup from the new bead 'A preflight-failed probe session is never cleared'. (3) CNF-14 (10:113-120, Astra) demands the source end below the sizing floor in ONE tick, while ADR-0029 expressly allows 'the source drains in several operations' and the fixture fixes neither fees nor viability — narrow the fixture to a route that drains in one operation, or assert progress over occurrences; review CNF-20 alongside. Owner for each: the scenario, citing the requirement it demonstrates.

title: FMI-41 / API-42: re-claim is reachable only once the contract is expired; funding expiry and claimability are conflated
description:
MAJOR, split from spec-cuw (Astra, Sol, Fable). 02-fedimint-integration.md:328-335 (FMI-41): a rejected claim MUST be retried until the contract's expiry has passed before the receive reaches Failure, and the explicit re-claim reports 'not claimable' when the contract is expired or already consumed. 04-api-contract.md:580-584 (API-42): {key} MUST name an operation whose incoming contract reached a terminal non-claim (Expired or Failed). So for the rejected-claim case the endpoint becomes invocable exactly when it must answer not_claimable; the accepted-claim-then-issuance-failed case (FMI-37, 02:320) has already consumed the contract. Stranded-via-Expired (the wallet's receive gave up before the gateway funded late) is still claimable, so reclaim is not useless in general — only for the rejected-claim case (Opus). Conflicts with CONTEXT.md:296 'A delayed app open does NOT forfeit an already-settled payment' and with the glossary's statement that a funded settled incoming contract does not expire in the ordinary invoice sense.
Protocol fact the fix rests on (Astra, from the local lnv2 server; the agent MUST re-verify in modules/fedimint-lnv2-server): the incoming output checks expiry when FUNDED; claiming an existing incoming contract does not apply that funding-expiry check. If so, FMI-41 must separate invoice/funding expiry from a funded contract's claimability, define a reachable recovery state (a claim rejected for reason X is retried; transient failure vs terminal), replay after a lost response, durable evidence of repeated successful re-claims, and API-42's precondition must admit that state. If not, the decision (what is recoverable at all) goes to 11-open-questions.md and FMI-41/API-42 stay silent. Owners: FMI-41, API-42, OPS-27; a scenario that demonstrates a SUCCESSFUL re-claim (a Stranded move followed by reclaim → claimed). spec-5gn's paid-orphan clause depends on this.

title: 'trusted' move record and 'probed' federation are used normatively and defined nowhere
description:
MAJOR, promoted from the minors by all four reviewers. (1) 'trusted': 03-operation-lifecycle.md:145-147 (OPS-9) 'The allocator projection weakens by move-record phase when the record is trusted'; 03:263 (OPS-45) skip pre-fund admission 'when the cached move record is trusted'; 03:633 (OPS-30) 'pristine (phase Created, trusted, …)'; 06:541-542 (ALC-35) 'A corrupt move record falls back to the strict projection'. CONTEXT.md has no entry; 05:209-239 (STO-11) has no trust rule; ADR-0024:41-43 lists 'Missing, corrupt, mismatched, oversized, or impossible' but no requirement does. Trust releases reservations (Sending drops the outbound) and skips admission, so the acceptance predicate changes money admission and /v1/status. Fix: STO-11 defines it from locally checkable correspondence — decodes, key equals the row key, to/from equal the action's, amount <= the action's, phase consistent with the artifacts (Sending/Settled/Stranded need send_op; Invoiced needs invoice + recv_op) — with fallback to the strict projection and the treatment of corrupt/stale records; OPS-9 owns the resulting projection; OPS-30, OPS-45, ALC-35 cite. (spec-dgj's rewritten skip keys on reassembled artifacts and so stops using the word there.)
(2) 'probed': 06:31 (ALC-1) 'whether it is probed'; 06:93 (ALC-5) 'not eligible to fund, or not probed (ALC-15)'; 06:491 (ALC-32) 'the number of probed federations'. Every snapshot member has passed the light probe, so 'probed' must mean something else — probably ALC-15's probe_gate_ok, but a successful light probe, an active-probe Passed verdict (ALC-25) and user approval (ALC-37) are different facts. Fix: define the snapshot field in ALC-1 by the exact predicate (ALC-25/ALC-37) and use it verbatim in ALC-5 and ALC-32; never substitute route validation for active-probe qualification. Both: add the terms to CONTEXT.md citing their owners.

title: Untyped persisted fields: WatchState (STO-12), EvacuationSupersessionRecord (STO-25), FederationInfo (STO-5) break upgrade-in-place
description: MAJOR, promoted from the minors (Opus, Astra, Sol; Fable keeps it minor). 05-persistence.md:241-242 (STO-12) WatchState fields carry no types: discover_backlog (bool? a count?), discover_rotation, last_discover_ms; 05:458-459 (STO-25) the sidecar fields old_attempt, refusal, old_cap_components?, … carry no types or domains; 05:83 (STO-5) FederationInfo {invite, db_prefix, joined_at (seconds)} gives no field types, and the InviteCode encoding is unstated because STO-5 says the string form appears 'only in CandidateRecord.invite' (FMI-20 contemplates an invite that does not parse). These are on-disk JSON under OVR-14's upgrade-in-place contract: two implementations can write bool against u8, or an id array against hex, and cannot read each other's stores. Fix: give every field a type, domain, optionality and STO-30 default, as STO-9, STO-15 and STO-26 do; do not claim types that are inferable elsewhere are unknown — complete the tables. Owners: STO-5, STO-12, STO-25, STO-30. (spec-nwm no longer owns FederationInfo's typing.)

title: User move / receive / direct-inflow have no default fee_cap, though the resolved value enters the operation key and admission
description: MAJOR, promoted from the minors by all four. 04-api-contract.md:265-266 (API-19): 'occurrence is required and, with the resolved fee_cap, is part of the operation key' — how fee_cap resolves is not stated; 04:294-297 (API-21): fee_cap? with no resolution rule; 04:576-578 (API-41) points back to 'the daemon-side policy defaults of API-18/API-19/API-21', but only API-18 (pay) states one ('fee_cap defaults to the policy's max_fee'). 01:124-126 (DOM-15): max_fee is 'absolute, for user verbs and probe legs' — the only hint. 03:597 (OPS-29) gives the Move row a base only for the allocator's stamp ('floor(amount × max_fee_bps_of_move / 10 000) stamped by the allocator, ALC-7'); a user move is not allocator-stamped. The default decides the move:<from>:<to>:<amount>:<fee_cap>:<occurrence> key (STO-6) and the money bound the wallet enforces, so two implementations derive different keys and pay different fees for the same request. Fix: API-19 and API-21 state 'fee_cap defaults to Policy.max_fee' (citing DOM-15); split OPS-29's Move row into a user row and an allocator row; API-41 and the CLI grammar (spec-ee9) cite it. One-line major.

title: ALC-29 auto-join counters (lifetime, weekly, concurrent_unproven) and ALC-28's rotation cursor are undefined
description: MAJOR, promoted from the minors (Opus, Astra, Sol). 06-allocator-and-automation.md:424-428 (ALC-29) gates auto-join on lifetime, weekly and concurrent_unproven without defining their populations (which rows: agent join:<fed>:<nonce> rows? excluding STO-35's re-open note? repaired rows? corrupt records?), the week boundary (rolling vs calendar, inclusivity — the 7-day window is defined only for probes, ALC-26), terminal statuses, or what 'unproven' means (AutoJoined not Passed?); 03:600-611 (OPS-42) supplies only one excluded no-op string; 05:582-594 (STO-22/STO-35) give ledger-scan hints only. 06:403-405 (ALC-28 step 3) takes 'a rotation window of max_candidates_per_pass from the stored cursor and rotation (STO-12)' without the cursor advancement or wrap rule. These decide which federations the agent joins, and 10:198-208 (CNF-17) exercises one successful auto-join, no limit. Fix: ALC-29 defines each count (counted events, durable source rows, time boundary, approval/probe transitions, reopen and failure treatment); ALC-28/STO-12 define exact cursor advancement and wrap; scenarios at, below and above every limit (in the coverage bead). Depends on spec-nwm (how agent-created vs user-created joins are durably identified).

title: A preflight-failed probe session is never cleared and its umbrella row never terminalizes: retained sessions starve fresh probes and hold budget
description: MAJOR, new finding (Opus), verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:361-367 (ALC-27): begin a session (STO-26); write the umbrella probe:<fed>:<nonce> row (STO-6); then preflight — 'where a failure is a no-attempt that changes no verdict'. 05-persistence.md:475-476 (STO-26): the session is 'cleared in the same transaction that appends the attempt' — a no-attempt appends nothing, so the session persists. 06:763-766 (ALC-52): 'Admission order: retained sessions first … If any retained session is admitted this cycle only the retained group is admitted and fresh probes are deferred' — one session whose preflight keeps failing (a source that cannot afford amount + leg_cap, an unopened candidate) starves every fresh probe indefinitely. 06:352-356 (ALC-26): 'active = uncosted non-terminal umbrella rows', 'retained while active || age < 7 d' — the row reserves budget with no age limit. STO-24 never repairs probe: rows. CNF-16's 'records nothing' (10:194-195) is wrong on the same facts (spec-pz6 fixes the assertion; the behaviour is decided here). Fix: ALC-27 states what a preflight failure does — clear the session and terminalize the umbrella row Failed with the reason (the pattern of OPS-35's 'no attempt recorded'), or retain it with an explicit retry bound — and STO-26, ALC-26, ALC-52 cite it; a scenario: candidate whose preflight fails twice, then a fresh probe of another candidate is admitted and the budget reflects no phantom reservation. Owner ALC-27.

title: Tick ledger order: ALC-4 says one tick's rows follow the emission order, ALC-53 writes the advisory refusal rows after the loop
description: MAJOR, new finding (Astra), verified. 06-allocator-and-automation.md:80-86 (ALC-4): 'The emission order is therefore: for each federation in snapshot order, its Evacuate or evacuation refusal, then the suppression twin …, then its advisory OverCap; then the spending step's decisions; then the standby step's … The ledger seq order of one tick's rows follows this order (ALC-34).' 06:794 (ALC-53): 'The advisory refusal rows are written after the loop'. An early federation's advisory followed by a later federation's evacuation yields opposite seq orders under the two rules; STO-18's counter fence forbids reserving seq holes to reconcile them. Observable on history. Fix: choose the observable row order under ALC-34 (emission order, or decisions-then-advisories) and align ALC-4 and ALC-53 without weakening the atomic intent/ledger admission; CNF-13's assertions follow. Owner ALC-34.

title: FMI-42 set-aside duration is 'a constant of the implementation': zero satisfies it and recreates the livelock ADR-0029 exists to stop
description: MAJOR, promoted from the minors (Opus, Sol; Astra keeps it minor). 02-fedimint-integration.md:202-211 (FMI-42): 'the skip-until duration is a constant of the implementation, not a Policy field'; ADR-0029:120-140 says only 'for a while'. A zero or negligible constant satisfies no stated predicate and the next attempt re-selects the pair that just failed to perform — the livelock ADR-0029 §3 names. It is also a prerequisite for a set-aside scenario (CNF-21 asserts only that a stall does not strand the move). Fix: FMI-42 states a positive minimum (or a bounded backoff), its clock semantics (monotonic, per process), and when the set-aside resets (a successful performance, a restart); extend CNF-21 with a second selection that avoids the pair within the interval. Owner FMI-42.

title: DOM-5 'exactly one current ledger row' vs OVR-4 best-effort rows that MAY be absent; ALC-44's stale-plan status failure has no API-15 code
description: MINOR pair, filed for completeness (Sol rates the first a blocker; Astra, Opus, Fable a scope clarification). (1) 01-domain-model.md:36-40 (DOM-5) 'Every operation has exactly one current ledger row'; 00-overview.md:36-44 (OVR-4): a row that describes no intent 'is written best-effort … MAY be absent after a storage error'; reclaim is an operation kind (API-42, STO-15) with no intent. Fix: qualify DOM-5 — intent-backed rows are guaranteed (STO-16), best-effort rows are 'an attempted operation whose row may be absent after a storage error' — or make the reclaim row a prerequisite of the attempt; do not turn every non-money row into an atomic record. (2) 06:660-663 (ALC-44): 'the resident host's status MUST fail with that error' for a stale replacement plan; 04:203-208 (API-15) 503 list is closed and does not include it; API-6 maps no other 5xx. Fix: add the condition and message to API-15's 503 list (or 409 conflict citing OPS-39) and clarify whole-probe failure vs a federation dropped under FMI-25. Owners DOM-5, OVR-4, API-15.

title: Conformance coverage: the scenarios no requirement cites (security, derivation vector, retry, watchdog, fences, budgets)
description:

Chapter 10 cites none of (verified by grep): FMI-40 (egress: a guardian-listed gateway at 169.254.169.254, at an RFC 1918 address, at a re-resolving DNS name, IPv4-mapped IPv6), API-2 / SEC-2 (401 before 404/405; constant-time compare needs review evidence, not a timing scenario — Astra), SEC-14 negative case (an override-served expiry alone never schedules), FMI-7 (a known-answer vector: fixed mnemonic + FederationId → expected client secret bytes, computed from the table at 02:57-64 AND cross-checked against the SDK's own derivation so a table error is not frozen — Opus; CNF-23 recovers on the same implementation, which proves nothing), OPS-10 (retry mints attempt 1, retry:<len>:<key>:<n> metadata), OPS-45, ALC-40 (watchdog trips, process exits non-zero), HST-19 (atomic secret files; CNF-54 covers part), HST-29, HST-33 (token/pointer mismatch), DOM-21 (probe/user key collision → 409), FMI-38 (5-minute bound), STO-18 (counter fence), ALC-30 / ALC-44 (suppression visible in status.suppressed; CNF-26 renders it without a fixture), API-35 (2 MiB body), OPS-46 / STO-24 (repair strings), ALC-26 (budget refusal), OPS-15 (perform timeout), OPS-7/OPS-9 refusals under concurrent admission, a Stranded move followed by a successful reclaim, goal-scoped suppression (ALC-30/DEF-6: a stuck move on one federation does not suppress another's evacuation), ALC-29 limits at/below/above each bound, FMI-42 set-aside (amend CNF-21), and the closed spec-bsd's residual: send issued, artifact write lost, send refunded, restart → no second contract (CNF-9).

Split the work by family when picking it up: (i) security/transport, (ii) the FMI-7 vector, (iii) retry/watchdog/host-failure/fences, (iv) allocator budgets and limits. Each scenario cites the requirement and the requirement cites it back (AGENTS.md). Depends on the behaviour beads listed below.
